dataset: Validation cases for a pipe-insulation heat-loss / heat-gain / condensation calculator (ASTM C680 / 3E Plus style), plus sourced service-temperature presets

conventions.unverified: The literal string 'unverified' means no fetched source stated the value. Nothing was guessed, averaged, interpolated or filled from memory. Where a value can only be obtained by a calculation (for example a unit conversion), the case says how, but does not print the computed number.
conventions.src: Every case and preset carries 'src', a list of ids in the top-level 'sources' array, plus a 'location' (page, table or figure).
conventions.quotes: 'quote' strings are verbatim from pdftotext output or page text. Line breaks and hyphenation were joined and runs of spaces collapsed; nothing else was changed. Fractions printed by pdftotext as '11/2' mean 1-1/2 and are written that way in transcribed values; the raw form is noted where it matters.
conventions.transcription: Large tables (V3 heat-transfer tables, V4 personnel-protection tables, V10/V11 ASHRAE tables, V23 NIST values) were parsed programmatically from the pdftotext -layout output or the HTML <table> markup, then spot-checked against the text. Smaller tables were hand-transcribed and machine-checked token by token against the source lines. Figure images (V16 Figure 1, V19 Figures 2 and 4) were read visually and are flagged as such.

units.temperature: °F unless a field name says otherwise
units.heat_loss_pipe: Btu/h per linear foot of pipe (Btu/hr·ft)
units.thickness: inches of insulation wall (nominal, as printed)

conventions.pipe_dimensions: NPS-to-OD (ASME B36.10M) and ASTM C585 insulation ODs are in research/pipe-dimensions.json and are not repeated here. A case lists pipe OD only when the source prints it.

dew_point_margin.text: 3E Plus and the NIA/MIDG condensation calculator report the condensation-control thickness as the first thickness whose surface temperature exceeds the dew point plus 0.75°F. ASHRAE Refrigeration Tables 3-12 state that they include no safety factor. Manufacturer tables from 3E Plus (V1) therefore embed the 0.75°F margin; tables whose engine is not stated have an unknown margin.

quotes.quote: The thickness that provides average surface temperature > Dew Point + a safety factor of 0.75°F
when performing condensation control calculations, 3ePlus includes a 0.75°F "safety factor" for the comparison of insulation system surface temperature to dew point.
Values do not include safety factor.

k_curve_in_3eplus.quote: 3ePlus allows only the use of a single 2nd order polynomial to model the curve.
k_curve_in_3eplus.note: Expect small differences against 3E Plus tables for closed-cell foams whose k(T) curve is not quadratic.

calculation_standard.text: All the 3E Plus and ASHRAE tables cite the ASTM C680 methodology. MIDG states the energy calculators use C680-10 algorithms; ASHRAE R22 cites C680-14; ASHRAE R26 cites "ASTM Standard C680 methodology" with no year.

emittance_reference.note: ASHRAE Fundamentals Table 16 'Emittance Data of Commonly Used Materials' (ε at ~80°F), transcribed for the defaults a calculator needs. These are generic values, not the inputs of any one case unless a case says so.

conventions.rounding_of_published_thickness: Published required thicknesses are rounded up to manufactured sizes (the step size differs by product and is visible in each table). A calculator should compare against the next available size, not the continuous thickness. MIDG/ASHRAE example: 1.29 in. computed, "rounded up to the next available size, probably 1.5 in."
conventions.comparison_tolerance_note: No source states a tolerance for reproducing its tables. Treat integer-rounded heat-loss values (V3) as ±0.5 of the last printed digit plus model differences (k-curve fit, C585 dimensions, convection correlation).
not_obtained: IECC 2021/2024 Table C403.12.3 on codes.iccsafe.org: a headless browser got a CAPTCHA page ("Help us verify real visitors"), which was not bypassed. WebFetch got HTTP 403.

ASHRAE 90.1-2019/2022 read-only viewer: needs an ASHRAE account login, which this agent may not create. The 90.1 fluid-temperature ranges come from the ASHRAE Fundamentals reproduction (V10 Table 3A) and the JM reproduction (V3).

FOAMGLAS condensation tables: none in the Owens Corning FOAMGLAS product guide (dms/10023979), FOAMGLAS ONE data sheet (dms/10024264) or FAQ (dms/10027074). ASHRAE R26 Tables 3-4 (cellular glass) stand in.

Current Armacell AP ArmaFlex pipe-size condensation table: not found. The current tube TDS (zoro/cloudfront copies) and the NA Application Manual have none. Only the 2010 flat-surface table (V8) was found.
Rockwool ProRox Process Manual: its jacket surface-temperature example is a bar chart with no printed values or ambient temperature, so it was not usable.
PermaTherm pipe thickness chart (arcat.com): Cloudflare challenge, not bypassed.

quotes.quote: Notes: Insulation thickness shown is that required to prevent condensation on outside jacket surface or limit heat gain to 8 Btu/h·ft2, whichever thickness is greater, at the conditions specified. Thicknesses shown are applicable only to the conditions specified. Changing any condition, even slightly, can influence the required thickness. All thicknesses are in inches. Values do not include safety factor. Actual operating conditions may vary. Consult a design engineer for appropriate recommendation for the specific system. Thickness calculated using ASTM Standard C680-23 methodology.

For insulation applied to cold pipe, it is more common to specify the insulation thickness that delivers a heat gain into the insulation system of 8 Btu/h · ft2 of outer jacket surface. This popular rule of thumb was used to generate Tables 3 to 12

notes: To validate condensation logic alone, a calculator must also apply the 8 Btu/h·ft² heat-gain criterion; at the indoor condition the heat-gain rule may govern for some cells. The source does not say which criterion governed each cell.
R26 Table 2 lists flexible elastomeric k at -50°F mean as 0.23; R22 listed 0.24. The Tables 3-12 thickness values are identical in both editions.
R26 Table 2 also adds Flexible Aerogel (ASTM C1728 Type I, Grade I, Category B; k 0.11 at -50 and 0°F, 0.12 at 75 and 120°F), but there is no aerogel thickness table.
